answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a small refundable stake, like a quartz deposit locked in escrow, before it may trade. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real money per identity, while honest agents recover their stake after clean behaviour. Reputation accrues slowly, like sediment turning to shale: a fresh sparrow with no history cannot outbid an established trader, so attackers must pay repeatedly and wait, which makes large-scale fakery unprofitable.
